missions.profile: Wide-field infrared survey telescope with a Hubble-class mirror but a field of view roughly one hundred times larger, built to study dark energy and find exoplanets through microlensing and direct imaging.
NASA/ESA/CSA infrared flagship observing from Sun–Earth L2, covering everything from the first galaxies to exoplanet atmospheres.
The veteran NASA/ESA optical and ultraviolet observatory in low Earth orbit, still producing frontline science in its fourth decade.
NASA's programme to return astronauts to the Moon with commercial and international partners. Artemis I flew uncrewed in 2022; Artemis II is the first crewed flight.
Europa Clipper is en route to assess the habitability of Jupiter's moon Europa, arriving in 2030; ESA's JUICE mission follows to the icy moons in 2031.
Parker Solar Probe flies repeated record-close passes through the Sun's corona to trace how the solar wind is heated and accelerated.
NASA's surface fleet — the Perseverance and Curiosity rovers — continues exploring Jezero and Gale craters, with orbiters relaying data overhead.
Continuously crewed orbital laboratory operated with international partners, hosting rotating crews and microgravity research.
Joint ESA/JAXA mission carrying two orbiters to Mercury. After an eight-year cruise it is now in its arrival phase, ahead of orbit insertion.
ESA's Earth-watching fleet: the Copernicus Sentinels monitor land, ocean and atmosphere, with FLEX next up to map plant fluorescence globally.
Solar Orbiter studies the Sun at close range and from progressively tilted orbits, returning the first good views of the solar poles.
India's human spaceflight programme, working toward its first crewed orbital mission through uncrewed test flights and recovery testing.
Earth observation satellite providing imaging over the Indian region from geostationary orbit.
India's heaviest operational launch vehicle, used for Chandrayaan-3 and slated for Gaganyaan, powered by the CE20 cryogenic upper stage.
China's robotic lunar programme. Chang'e-6 returned the first far-side samples in 2024; Chang'e-7 and -8 target the lunar south pole ahead of a planned research station.
China's planetary exploration line: Tianwen-1 orbits Mars, Tianwen-2 is en route to sample the quasi-satellite Kamo'oalewa, and Tianwen-3 aims to return samples from Mars.
8.4-metre survey telescope in Chile with the largest digital camera ever built, imaging the entire southern sky every few nights.

items.title: China postpones Chang'e-7 lunar south pole mission
items.summary: China has postponed the Chang'e-7 mission to the lunar south pole, prompting analysis of what the delay and a wider reorganization mean for its lunar exploration programme.

items.summary: Did you spend part of your summer camping, hiking, at the pool, or in an aircraft? So did NASA’s 2025 Astronaut Candidate Class. items.title: Roman Space Telescope launches from Florida and begins commissioning
items.summary: NASA's Nancy Grace Roman Space Telescope lifted off from Florida and has begun spacecraft commissioning. Roman pairs a Hubble-sized mirror with a field of view roughly one hundred times larger for wide-field infrared surveys.

items.title: How Roman will find exoplanets — and what it can do that Hubble cannot
items.summary: Roman will detect distant planets by gravitational microlensing — gravity acting as a magnifying glass — and directly image others with its coronagraph. Its 300-megapixel Wide Field Instrument drives survey studies of dark energy and exoplanet demographics.

items.title: ISRO successfully conducts 2nd integrated air drop test for Gaganyaan mission | Akashvani News
items.summary: ISRO successfully conducted its second integrated air drop test for the Gaganyaan human spaceflight programme.

items.title: ESA Space Environment Report 2026
items.summary: ESA published its 2026 Space Environment Report, its annual accounting of debris and traffic in Earth orbit.

items.title: FLEX and Sentinel-3C ready for a shared launch on Vega-C
items.summary: ESA's FLEX mission — designed to map the faint fluorescent glow of photosynthesising plants — and the Copernicus Sentinel-3C satellite are ready for liftoff on a single Vega-C flight, with ESA mission control rehearsing the unusual dual launch.

items.title: Parker Solar Probe checks in healthy after latest close pass of the Sun
items.summary: NASA's Parker Solar Probe reported back in good health following its latest perihelion pass, continuing its record-setting series of close approaches to the Sun.

items.title: NASA's Chandra Spots Galactic Gem
items.summary: Galaxies are like cosmic gems, each with characteristics including size and shape that make them distinct. A gallery from NASA’s Chandra X-ray Observatory and other telescopes displays a collection of galactic images that showcase this variety.

items.title: Europa Clipper: Your Guide to Assembly
items.summary: A NASA guide to how Europa Clipper — the largest spacecraft the agency has built for a planetary mission — was assembled, now en route to Jupiter's moon Europa.

items.title: Dust and Water in Sagittarius A*
items.summary: Using the James Webb Space Telescope, an international team of astronomers have discovered that dust and water can form and survive surprisingly close to the supermassive black hole at the center of our Milky Way galaxy.

items.title: CE20 cryogenic engine hot-fired at 220 kN for LVM3 M7 mission
items.summary: ISRO successfully hot-tested its CE20 cryogenic upper-stage engine at a 220 kN thrust level ahead of the LVM3 M7 mission.

items.title: China alters Chang’e-8 lunar south pole mission amid lunar program reorganization
items.summary: China has altered its Chang'e-8 lunar south pole mission as part of a wider reorganization of its lunar programme.

items.title: Artemis II Crew at NASA Marshall
items.summary: The crew of NASA’s Artemis II mission visited NASA’s Marshall Space Flight Center in Huntsville, Alabama on Sept. 1, 2026.

items.title: BepiColombo begins Mercury arrival with successful transfer module separation
items.summary: After an eight-year cruise, the joint ESA/JAXA BepiColombo mission separated from its Mercury Transfer Module, beginning arrival operations ahead of orbit insertion. ESA also released the module's selfie footage spanning the journey.

items.title: China on track to launch Mars sample-return mission in 2028: 'If accurate, this represents a Sputnik moment'
items.summary: Chinese officials say the Tianwen-3 Mars sample-return mission remains on track for a 2028 launch — a timeline some observers describe as a potential 'Sputnik moment'.

items.title: Superbubble in the Large Magellanic Cloud
items.summary: N44 is a complex nebula filled with glowing hydrogen gas, dark lanes of dust, massive stars, and many populations of stars of different ages. One of its most distinctive features, however, is the dark, starry gap called a “superbubble,” visible in this Hubble Space Telescope image in the upper central region.

items.title: An Early Discovery by Rubin Observatory!
items.summary: Astronomers report one of the first scientific discoveries made with early Vera C. Rubin Observatory survey data.

items.title: Anak Krakatau eruption by Sentinel-3
items.summary: Image: Copernicus Sentinel-3 captured a plume from the eruption of Anak Krakatau on Saturday, 5 September.

items.title: EOS-05 Mission: ISRO Says Final Orbit-Raising Manoeuvre Successful, Satellite Now In Geostationary Orbit
items.summary: ISRO's EOS-05 Earth observation satellite completed its final orbit-raising manoeuvre and is now in geostationary orbit.

items.title: ISRO, IN-SPACe Face Rocket Transfer Row
items.summary: Reports describe a disagreement between ISRO and the space regulator IN-SPACe over transferring rocket technology to private industry.

items.title: This is the first ever close-up image of Earth’s ‘mini moon’. We could soon have samples back on Earth
items.summary: China released the first-ever close-up image of Kamo'oalewa, Earth's quasi-satellite 'mini moon' and the sample-return target of the Tianwen-2 spacecraft.
